transcript: I'll never do business with a client unless they hit these three checkpoints. And if you skip this before you pitch anyone with your AI automations, you're going to be wasting months chasing the wrong businesses. I run them through three checkpoints. First, has the business actually been running five years or more? A business with that kind of track record already has systems, a customer base, cash flow. They're not gonna disappear on you mid-project, and you've got the stability to actually invest in something new. Second, are they actively spending money? That can be running ads, doing SEO, paying for marketing in some form. This matters because it proves two things: they've got a budget to spend, and they've already got a flow of leads coming in that your AI service can plug into. Third, what's their average sale value? You see, I'm looking for businesses where a single sale is worth $3,000 or more. If the business only makes a small profit per customer, you're going to have to help them make tons of sales with your AI, which is still possible, it's just much harder. But if one single sale is worth thousands, I mean, a roofing job's worth $100,000 sometimes. You're only going to have to get them one extra customer to make you look like a hero and a no-brainer to continue. Meanwhile, niches like roofing, solar, high-ticket services, one job, as I said, can be worth between five and a $100,000, even more. So you only need to land them a couple of extra jobs and they're thrilled to keep paying you. Established, already spending on leads, big enough sales value. That's my criteria.
